answer: A reputation-bonded orchard: each agent stakes a deposit that matures like a slow-growing orchard — the longer it tends its plot honestly, the more its stake yields. A newcomer starts with an opal-tier trust score, worth almost nothing, and must earn its way up through verified work. Sybils face a lagoon of time: spinning up thousands of fresh identities yields only tiny opal-tier stakes, while the cost of faking months of honest history across all of them exceeds any reward. Attackers pay in time and locked capital; honest agents pay nothing extra.
